 MISSOULA, Mont. — The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission announced two recalls Nov. 5 involving millions of ladders and thousands of air fryer ovens because of fall and burn hazards.
 Little Giant Ladder Systems is recalling about 3.66 million ladders equipped with Rapid Locks because they can suddenly retract if the locks are not fully engaged, posing a fall hazard.
 The company has received 25 reports of ladders retracting, including 19 injuries.
 The recall includes Adjustable Fortress 2.0, Conquest 2.0, Dark Horse 2.0, Epic, King Kombo XT, Leveler, MegaLite, MegaLite+, Multi, Quantum and Vector models that do not have an orange rectangular "QC" sticker on the rail above a Rapid Lock.
 The ladders were sold at Lowe's, Costco and other retailers nationwide, as well as online, from December 2015 through October 2026 for approximately $100 to $1,000.
 Consumers should stop using affected ladders until they review the company's instructions and contact Little Giant for a repair kit. If a lock continues to malfunction after inspection and lubrication, the company may offer a replacement or refund.
 Gourmia is also recalling about 176,000 stainless-steel 9-slice digital air fryer ovens because the doors can unexpectedly swing shut when bumped, posing a burn hazard.
 The recall involves model GTF7530.
 The company has received 57 reports of doors closing while consumers were retrieving food, resulting in 40 hand or wrist burns.
 The ovens were sold at Target stores nationwide and online at Target.com from October 2021 through June 2026 for approximately $150.
 Consumers should stop using the recalled ovens and contact Gourmia for a free repair kit that includes a doorstop and installation instructions.
